intro: Three 3.14 features are especially useful in engineering code: t-strings (PEP 750) let interpolations be handled safely, annotations are now evaluated lazily (PEP 649/749), and the standard library gains Zstandard compression (PEP 784).
example_title: t-string parameterised SQL, deferred annotations and zstd
example_desc: A t-string does not produce a str but a Template; to_sql() replaces every interpolation with ? and moves the value into a parameter list, so hostile input is treated purely as data. poll()'s annotations can name classes that do not exist yet. zstd compresses highly repetitive CSV records.

case.title: A point name with an apostrophe breaks the query
paragraphs: A reporting tool built SQL with f-strings and failed as soon as the point name O'Neil_AHU appeared; with web input, injection is the bigger risk. An f-string mixes value and SQL the moment it is created, so no function downstream can tell them apart. A t-string keeps the structure and lets a processing function decide how each interpolation is handled.

Lazy annotations remove the need for from __future__ import annotations or string annotations when modules reference each other's types, and zstd makes archive compression available without a third-party package.
steps: Always parameterise database queries; a t-string with a processing function is one way to wrap this.
Find code that relies on __annotations__ being evaluated eagerly and switch it to annotationlib.
Evaluate zstd for log and history archives, comparing ratio and speed.
Run the full test suite on 3.14 before upgrading.

updates.text: Python 3.14 is in full (bugfix) support; extension output was rechecked on 3.14.10. 3.14.5 reverted the incremental garbage collector.

sources.title: Python Developer's Guide: Status of Python versions

exercises.q: What is the key difference between t"..." and f"..."?
exercises.a: An f-string produces a str immediately. A t-string produces a Template that keeps the static strings and every interpolation (value, expression, conversion and format spec), so a processing function can decide how to combine them, for example by escaping or parameterising.

exercises.q: Does print(t"...") print the combined string?
exercises.a: No, it prints the Template's repr. Templates deliberately have no default string conversion; a processing function must render them, which prevents unsafe direct use.

exercises.q: What happens if the example's poll() definition runs on 3.13?
exercises.a: NameError: GatewayDevice is not defined. Before 3.14 annotations were evaluated when the function was defined, unless from __future__ import annotations or string annotations were used.

exercises.q: Why does the example compress so well?
exercises.a: The data is one line repeated 2,000 times and carries almost no information. Real time-series data repeats less, so measure with your own data; zstd's strength is being faster than gzip at a similar ratio.
